statusDetail: Target edge denied both Chrome and direct HTTP access with HTTP 403 (rps: w403). Only the branded error document was rendered, so representative templates and core flows could not be audited.

page.notes: The delivered 403 error document contains legacy React markers, but the production application was not reachable and no framework inference is made.

artifacts.caption: Desktop entry navigation shows the Mercado Libre 403 error state.
Mobile entry navigation shows the same 403 error state and lacks a viewport meta tag.
Dark-preference capture is still the edge error state, not the production surface.
Rendered DOM is the edge error document, with no title, lang, viewport, production navigation, or forms.
Layout metrics for the edge error document only.
Ad-hoc DOM and platform probe confirms only the error page was available.
Security headers observed on the 403 response; not treated as production-page evidence.
Raw-fetch/render comparison; browser render remained blocked while a crawler-like raw fetch received different content.
artifacts.condition: crawler raw fetch versus browser render

artifacts.caption: Browser-side rendered screenshot from discoverability capture shows the edge error.
No-JavaScript browser screenshot also shows the edge error.
HAR records four requests, including two HTTP 403 responses.
Compact HAR summary records status breakdown 200:2 and 403:2.
Pre-evidence atomic coverage manifest and per-check evidence plan.
Atomic coverage validator output showing 58 blocked checks and no missing, unknown, or duplicate rows.
